features.description: Specify the reviewed iklib pilot and its two-game quality and adoption criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Carry forward curated upstream plus authored gaps, iklib first, project independence and verified pinned capability adoption with optional IDE/shared harness; record remaining wrapper, infrastructure and training boundaries explicitly.
Specify the selected iklib core proof in VtMB and NOLF with exact target profiles, parity measures, resource budgets and bounded effort; preserve separate finger migrations.
Review the revised library-first proposal and record accepted scope before activating features.json.
features.deliverable: docs/specs/001-library-pilot.md

features.description: Specify a project adapter contract that preserves native commands and policies.
acceptance_criteria: Versioned schema represents repository identity, game target, progress/inventory paths, argv commands, working directory, verification tiers and capabilities.
Fixtures represent reLith NOLF/AVP2/NOLF2 and reSource without forcing common paths, ECS, SDL or CMake targets.
Reject malformed commands, missing required identities and unknown required contract versions; inspection does not execute commands.
features.deliverable: contracts/project-v1.schema.json and fixtures

features.description: Specify a verification result envelope with honest non-pass states.
acceptance_criteria: Contract records pass, fail, skip, infrastructure_error, timeout and pending_manual distinctly, with declared required checks.
Each check identifies command, tool/host revision, platform/profile, timestamps, raw-log reference and reason for a non-pass.
Negative fixtures prove that missing/skipped required checks and absent manual evidence cannot aggregate to passing.
features.deliverable: contracts/check-result-v1.schema.json and fixtures

features.description: Implement one local native-command runner with bounded process lifetime.
acceptance_criteria: Execute argv directly in an explicit workspace; preserve native exit status, stdout and stderr without shell interpolation.
Real child-process tests cover success, nonzero exit, timeout including child cleanup, missing executable and explicit skip mapping.
Inspection/plan mode performs no execution; first runner scope is the pilot platform from F1, with unsupported platforms reported explicitly.
features.deliverable: runner implementation and process integration evidence

features.description: Write immutable, verifiable run bundles from runner results.
acceptance_criteria: Bundle includes source revision plus dirty patch identity when relevant, adapter/tool version, declared check inventory, results and hashed logs.
Writes are atomic and existing run identities cannot be silently overwritten; partial/interrupted runs remain visibly incomplete.
Validator rejects tampered/missing artifacts and path traversal; valid bundle survives relocation without absolute sibling paths.
features.deliverable: run-bundle contract, writer and validator

features.description: Describe and exercise the selected reLith check through a local adapter.
acceptance_criteria: Resolve current native check command from the host and identify NOLF, AVP2 and NOLF2 separately; use the F1-selected pilot target only.
In a prepared isolated host workspace, direct and wrapped invocation agree on results and relevant raw facts.
Adapter preserves source/assets identity and host gate requirements; it never changes the original host tracker or active worktree.
features.deliverable: adapters/relith pilot and run evidence

features.description: Describe and exercise the selected reSource check through a local adapter.
acceptance_criteria: Resolve the selected native check from the current host; encode everyday/slow/data/manual tiers without weakening required gates.
In a prepared isolated host workspace, direct and wrapped invocation agree without assuming reLith paths or binaries.
Record missing assets/tools as non-passes and leave the original host tracker and active worktree untouched.
features.deliverable: adapters/resource pilot and run evidence

features.description: Demonstrate the same tool on both real engine pilots.
acceptance_criteria: Archive validated bundles from actual native invocations in both selected engine snapshots and compare with their direct baselines.
Demonstrate at least one intentional non-pass that remains non-passing through aggregation; infrastructure problems are not hidden.
Record wrapper overhead and outcome preservation against direct native invocation; justify further tooling adoption from the actual integration needs. Fixtures alone do not complete this feature.
features.deliverable: docs/evidence/first-two-engine-proof.md

features.description: Package a minimal agent-neutral harness template with local policy extension.
acceptance_criteria: Generate a usable instruction entry point, single progress log, feature helper, spec template and bootstrap in a temporary repository.
Project-specific rules extend the template without replacing the host authority; optional agent entry points reference the same instructions.
Generated repository boots without other game repositories or network; template update produces an explicit reviewable diff.
features.deliverable: templates/minimal and generated fixture repository

features.description: Adopt a pinned rEngine tool capability in the reLith workspace.
acceptance_criteria: Host owner records an approved integration task and adopts a reviewed immutable tool version with a local adapter.
Existing feature IDs, descriptions, progress history and required game gates remain authoritative; host selected checks pass.
Demonstrate the adopted workflow in an independent checkout without rEngine sibling path; report capability and game target scope.
features.deliverable: host-owned spec, pin/adapter commit and gate evidence

features.description: Adopt a pinned rEngine tool capability in the reSource workspace.
acceptance_criteria: Host owner records an approved integration task and adopts a reviewed immutable tool version with a local adapter.
Preserve local verification tiers, progress history, device/manual requirements and ordinary build behavior.
Demonstrate the adopted workflow in an independent checkout without rEngine sibling path; record selected platform/profile scope.
features.deliverable: host-owned spec, pin/adapter commit and gate evidence

features.description: Prove independent tool upgrade and rollback in both consumers.
acceptance_criteria: Use host-owned evidence to show one consumer upgrades while the other remains on its reviewed version.
Both accepted versions pass their declared contract/gates; incompatible contract is rejected with an actionable reason.
Restore the preceding pin/adapter and reproduce the relevant gate; no synchronized game release is required.
features.deliverable: docs/evidence/tool-upgrade-rollback.md

features.description: Define the catalog admission and compatibility record for real components.
acceptance_criteria: Owner decides required provenance/license documentation, maintainer, immutable source identity, capability, platforms and independent-consumption evidence.
Schema distinguishes discovered candidate, reviewed recipe and verified consumer adoption; none implies another.
Represent iklib and infra-vr from current source evidence; a hypothetical flecs choice is not marked selected or verified.
features.deliverable: catalog schema and admission policy

features.description: Define reproducible dependency pins and explicit developer overrides.
acceptance_criteria: Choose one consumption mechanism with owner input at F1/F13 and test immutable revision/checksum resolution.
Consumer fixture builds from prepared local sources without implicit home paths or hidden network; missing material fails explicitly.
Local source override is opt-in and appears in evidence; it cannot be advertised as the reviewed release pin.
features.deliverable: dependency manifest/lock contract and consumer fixtures

features.description: Publish a reviewed local iklib consumption recipe and two fixture proofs.
acceptance_criteria: Use the actual iklib CMake target and supported source-tree model at a reviewed revision; do not invent an install package.
Two minimal host-shaped fixtures with different frames/scales compile and run selected solvers without unrelated engine dependencies.
Verify consumer target/options/test isolation; recipe links pending host migrations and makes no completed-game-integration claim.
features.deliverable: catalog/iklib entry and consumption evidence

features.description: Resolve the infra-vr embeddable packaging boundary from both host closures.
acceptance_criteria: Pin and compare both actual INFRA_VR_DIR build closures, target/option collisions, microui ownership and optional transport/platform dependencies.
Agree with the owner whether the fix belongs upstream in infra-vr or in a narrowly scoped consumption recipe; name files and rollback.
Specify both consumer fixture builds and acceptance conditions; do not operate or redesign the backend.
features.deliverable: docs/specs/016-infra-packaging.md

features.description: Prove pinned infra-vr consumption with both host-shaped build fixtures.
acceptance_criteria: Implement the reviewed recipe or consume its owner-landed upstream change at an immutable pin.
Both fixtures build the reporting ABI with one microui definition and no leaked parent options/targets or implicit sibling path.
Exercise a local synthetic report/render callback path and explicit transport configuration; retain upstream-change references if required.
features.deliverable: catalog/infra-vr recipe and fixture evidence

features.description: Complete the existing reSource core IK migration from its owning workspace.
acceptance_criteria: Re-pin current host seam, map a host-owned feature to iklib:F131, and satisfy its unchanged acceptance criteria.
Record old/new pose equivalence and existing IK/contract tests using the pinned library; remove obsolete core solver code.
Record relevant host runtime/manual gates and rollback; do not claim the separate finger migration is included.

features.description: Complete the existing reLith IK migration with NOLF parameter parity.
acceptance_criteria: Resolve iklib F130 V2 constant comparison against current host before changing solver behavior; use explicit per-host parameters if needed.
Complete F130 criteria with existing host tests and recorded old/new output equivalence; remove replaced production solvers.
Record every reLith game affected by the shared closure, required gates and rollback; adding fingers is a separate task.
features.deliverable: host migration commit and iklib:F130 evidence link

features.description: Complete the separate reSource finger IK migration.
acceptance_criteria: Map the engine-side finger seam outside src/vrik to the existing iklib:F133 scope.
Prove recorded curl/collision/pose behavior equivalence and host gates; remove or reduce duplicate glm solver code to necessary glue.
Retain separate device/manual evidence where required; no NOLF finger capability is claimed.
Update the adoption matrix with separately verified finger rows; the core two-game proof does not depend on this follow-up.
features.deliverable: host finger migration commit and iklib:F133 evidence link

features.description: Record runtime adoption evidence by engine, game and supported profile.
acceptance_criteria: Reference both core host migrations F18/F19 and immutable evidence without changing external feature states; list fingers pending until separately proven by F20 or its host-owned follow-up.
Distinguish NOLF, AVP2, NOLF2 and VtMB plus flat/VR/platform profiles; list verified, unaffected, pending or unsupported honestly.
Each verified row includes component revision, host gates and rollback evidence; coordinate optional iklib:F132 as separate future work.
For the first library proof, retain host integration effort, replaced production duplication and representative resource evidence; evaluate the agreed F1/F31 quality measures.
features.deliverable: docs/evidence/ik-adoption-matrix.md

features.description: Define report-to-reproduction metadata around existing infra-vr reports.
acceptance_criteria: Record report/game/build identity, archived save/input hashes, reproduction steps and expected observation without redefining report transport.
Fixtures distinguish restricted/local assets from exportable metadata and do not embed credentials or game content.
A valid reference resolves to the original local evidence; missing/changed save identity cannot masquerade as a reproduced bug.
features.deliverable: report/repro contract and synthetic fixtures

features.description: Represent oracle and manual/device evidence without replacing native gates.
acceptance_criteria: Record original-reference version, capture/replay identity, declared tolerance or manual criterion, observer and result.
Demonstrate that unit tests cannot substitute for pending visual/audio/headset criteria and that absent reference is non-passing.
Round-trip representative reLith and reSource evidence shapes without introducing a shared game-format parser.
features.deliverable: oracle/manual evidence extension and fixtures

features.description: Specify an explicit eligibility-checked development evidence export.
acceptance_criteria: Map only allowed development evidence to the current training schemas, preserving source/tool revisions and content hashes.
Reject held-out repository/task identity, withheld fixes/tests, missing provenance and tampered artifacts; ordinary indexes expose no grader material.
Training owner reviews boundary and downstream task; output carries eligibility/outcome rather than invented reward or solved status.
features.deliverable: export contract, classifier fixtures and training mapping spec

features.description: Demonstrate the evidence bridge in the training-owned intake path.
acceptance_criteria: Execute a synthetic eligible export through the actual training intake validation path and preserve all provenance fields.
Frozen/hidden/tampered negative examples fail before ingestion; grader isolation and split authority remain in training.
Record exact versions and results; do not start training, change eval selections or bypass F30 and owner GO.
features.deliverable: training-owned intake spec and synthetic E2E evidence

features.description: Coordinate explicitly reserved workspaces and scarce test resources.
acceptance_criteria: Use explicit resource IDs for workspace/build directory, display or device; avoid global host discovery.
Two competing processes prove exclusive ownership, reliable release after failure, and safe stale-owner recovery without stealing active work.
Planning and CPU-only use require no device; reservation does not grant launch, deployment or production authority.
features.deliverable: local reservation contract and contention tests

features.description: Map both games' library needs and qualify the selected iklib pilot scope.
acceptance_criteria: Map relevant existing dependencies and duplicated capabilities across both games with current source references and actual integration differences.
For the initial scope, classify curate upstream, extract our own component, implement a demonstrated gap or keep host-local; do not mark untested candidates qualified.
Use owner-selected iklib for the first two-game core proof; record exact integration slices, quality gaps and bounded follow-ups, preserving independent iklib/infra-vr ownership.
features.deliverable: docs/library-coverage.md and first-candidate decision

features.description: Prove a new host can adopt a capability without either game engine.
acceptance_criteria: Create a minimal unrelated host layout/object model that consumes one selected capability using public interfaces only.
No reLith/reSource source, globals, game assets or mandatory ECS are needed; remove either game adapter and the fixture still works.
Document what a future flecs-based host would own without claiming or adding a flecs integration absent a selected consumer.
features.deliverable: independent host fixture and conformance evidence

features.description: Define evidence-backed powered-by records for both engine families.
acceptance_criteria: Apply D24: at least one curated capability at a pinned version with passing game integration checks; list exact capabilities, pins and verified game/platform/profile rows.
Keep IDE/shared harness use optional and upgrades independent; include only separately proven tool/runtime capabilities without requiring the later shared-runner branch.
Do not relabel a pending host, publish branding changes or require an unrelated component to claim a verified capability.
features.deliverable: docs/compatibility.md and adoption record format

features.description: Audit the harness and decide the next bounded roadmap from measured results.
acceptance_criteria: Validate feature graph, local document links, source/evidence freshness and owner-workspace boundaries; record drift with repair actions.
Compare first-library integration benefit, resource measurements and maintenance cost against F1/F31 measures, including failed and deferred verification.
Review the next bounded work with the owner; preserve accepted feature history and the confirmed independent library/workspace paths instead of expanding unrelated runtime scope.
features.deliverable: docs/audits/first-cycle.md and reviewed follow-up proposal

features.description: Agree the library quality standard and the usable integration knowledge package.
acceptance_criteria: Owner reviews applicable correctness, API/ownership/threading, composition, resource, portability, maintenance and agent-usability criteria; requirements remain scoped per component.
Distinguish candidate, qualified component and verified real-consumer adoption with explicit evidence for each claim.
Apply the standard to the selected first library and define the minimum executable examples, contract context, native checks, measurements and failure cases before integration.
features.deliverable: docs/library-quality.md and selected-library qualification spec

features.description: Specify the first desktop workspace, terminal, draft recovery and NOLF integration slice.
acceptance_criteria: Carry forward macOS/Windows, empty-to-split layout, movable tabs, basic editing/optional Vim, persistent sidecar sessions, the session browser and multiple project/worktree roots with explicit per-session bindings as confirmed requirements.

Pin the owner-selected flat NOLF host build/profile; specify actual rendered output/input in a new tab, native host ownership and acceptance commands on both platforms, with VtMB as the second adapter.

Specify stable root identities and local recovery drafts with explicit file saves; define checkpoint/conflict handling, initial Vim subset and predeclared measurable terminal/editor/game budgets; keep agent installers, Quest and XR as later gates.
features.deliverable: docs/specs/032-desktop-v0.md

features.description: Qualify the desktop UI, terminal and game-surface stack on macOS and Windows.
acceptance_criteria: Compare a small set of existing layout/editor/terminal components against native desktop and later Quest-client constraints with source/license/version references.
On both platforms demonstrate a real PTY, editable text/Vim-mode feasibility and a real cooperative graphical surface with resize/input; static mockups are insufficient.
Measure agreed budgets and choose an implementation stack with known limits and rollback; failure produces a revised proposal, not a supported-platform claim.
features.deliverable: docs/decisions/desktop-stack.md and bounded feasibility prototype

features.description: Implement the empty workspace with recursive splits and movable tab groups.
acceptance_criteria: Start empty, split horizontally/vertically, resize and collapse splits, and open/reorder/move tabs between pane groups.
Keyboard/pointer focus follows the intended tab; moving a view preserves its session and root binding and does not trigger a new session or change another tab's context.
Exercise the actual UI on macOS and Windows, including minimum sizes and displays with different scaling.
features.deliverable: orchestrator layout implementation and UI evidence

features.description: Implement a desktop sidecar that owns interactive sessions independently of views.
acceptance_criteria: Session records identify owning sidecar, stable project/worktree root, type, target, launch cwd, process/PTY identity and state; launch only through explicit commands and distinguish shell cwd from launch association.
Closing a view or GUI leaves sessions alive; reconnect attaches to the same session; explicit Stop terminates the intended process tree and reports exit.

Test sessions in two separate worktrees, GUI loss, sidecar failure, missing roots and stale identities on macOS/Windows; never retarget a session by focus/display name or claim a terminated process has resumed.
features.deliverable: sidecar session service and lifecycle tests

features.description: Connect real terminal panes to sidecar-owned PTY sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Exercise an interactive shell/full-screen terminal program with input, resize, scrollback, Unicode, paste and control keys on both desktops.

Move/detach/reattach terminals bound to different roots without losing their process and retained output; focus routes input only to the selected session and a shell cwd change does not rebind its launch root.
Long-lived sessions have no inherited verification-job deadline; measure responsiveness and retain failure/exit state.
features.deliverable: terminal provider and desktop acceptance evidence

features.description: Provide project tree, previews and basic text editing with optional Vim mode.
acceptance_criteria: Browse multiple declared roots, preview files, and edit/save text with undo/redo/search, dirty-buffer status and external-change handling; identical relative filenames in separate worktrees retain distinct root-bound buffers and save destinations.
Exercise the F32-defined Vim subset and ordinary editing on macOS/Windows; preserve supported encoding/line endings and avoid silent overwrite of external edits.

Retain unsaved edits as local recovery drafts on view close/GUI restart and write working files only on explicit Save; exercise external edits, checkpoint failure and explicit Discard without losing the only unsaved copy; large/binary/unsupported files fail or preview explicitly.
features.deliverable: file/tree/editor providers and edit-path evidence

features.description: Persist layout and recover views onto retained sessions after GUI restart.
acceptance_criteria: Restore splits, tab placement, stable root/session associations and durable local editor drafts after closing/reopening the GUI with multiple projects/worktrees; no restore path silently writes working files.
Resolve live session IDs through the sidecar; no restore path relaunches commands automatically or confuses a dead process with a live one.

Interrupted saves and unknown persistence versions recover with an actionable result; test macOS/Windows paths and changed/missing/removed roots without silently remapping sessions, relaunching commands or stopping retained processes.
features.deliverable: versioned workspace persistence and recovery evidence

features.description: Implement the terminal-based Bash agent selector and extensible launch registry.
acceptance_criteria: Discover supported installed CLI agents and allow an explicit custom installed command; launch in the chosen terminal's explicit root and launch directory regardless of another tab's focused project.
Keep recipes/version detection outside pane code and specify the Windows Bash/native-or-WSL path contract without guessing conversions.
Prove selection/launch both inside the orchestrator and standalone on macOS/Windows, including missing agent and cancelled selection.
features.deliverable: standalone agent launcher and registered CLI recipes

features.description: Add visible selected-agent installation and recoverable setup recipes.
acceptance_criteria: For a user-selected supported recipe, show official source, version, destination and required changes before installation; do not install on tab open alone.
Verify the installed CLI/version and support cancellation, failed download/install and repeat invocation without corrupting an existing installation.
Exercise at least the first agreed real CLI recipe per desktop platform plus isolated failure fixtures; preserve unrelated agent configuration.
features.deliverable: versioned agent install recipes and installation evidence

features.description: Bootstrap project MCP integrations through agent-specific configuration adapters.
acceptance_criteria: Merge the explicitly bound root's project profile through the supported CLI/version adapter without replacing unrelated settings, using a global active project or assuming every agent shares a format.
Distinguish configured, reachable, unsupported and failed integrations; re-running setup is idempotent and exposes repair steps.
Prove the selected agent calls an actual local test MCP tool scoped to its project/session; unknown CLI configuration is not silently guessed.
features.deliverable: agent integration profiles and connectivity evidence

features.description: Implement the cooperative game surface and input contract for desktop panes.
acceptance_criteria: Transport actual frames from a separate graphical process to a tab with explicit session identity, frame lifetime, resize and input semantics.
Prove focus/aspect/DPI handling, view movement, detach/reattach and explicit stop without affecting another session on macOS and Windows.
Measure the F32/F33 budgets and keep the transport distinct from MCP control; expose capabilities suitable for a later remote client.
features.deliverable: versioned surface adapter and native graphical fixture

features.description: Render flat NOLF into an orchestrator tab on macOS and Windows.
acceptance_criteria: From the owning nolf-improved workspace, implement the flat NOLF adapter using the F32-pinned native build/launch profile and user-owned assets.
Show actual game output in a new tab and verify resize, input, tab move, close/reattach and explicit stop through the sidecar on macOS and Windows.
Run relevant existing host gates, record the tested game/profile and rollback; an external window or log-only tab does not complete the pane requirement.
features.deliverable: reLith-owned surface adapter and two-platform game evidence

features.description: Add the reSource flat-game surface through the same public session contract.
acceptance_criteria: Implement a host-owned adapter without importing reLith engine/window types or requiring its dependencies.
Exercise actual VtMB rendering/input/resize/reattach on the declared desktop profiles with the same public surface contract.
Preserve the existing host gates and record unsupported/pending profiles separately; verify game behavior and rollback.
features.deliverable: reSource-owned adapter and scoped compatibility evidence

features.description: Host one additional rendered tool through an explicit pane provider.
acceptance_criteria: Select a real tool need and qualify its native or web presentation route against the agreed stack; no assumption all tools share one renderer.
Open, move, resize and close/reopen its pane with project/session identity and honest lifecycle/error state.
Record input capabilities and limitations; tool-specific UI types do not enter the game runtime contract.
features.deliverable: tool provider contract and one real tool integration

features.description: Resolve Meta XR Operator compatibility for a selected native host profile.
acceptance_criteria: Verify current standalone layer/proxy/custom-tool documentation and pin selected host OpenXR loader, graphics binding and runtime profile.
Define session targeting, endpoint coexistence, input ownership and native custom-tool boundaries; do not inherit Unity scene capabilities by assertion.
Specify one real native read/capture/input proof and cleanup path; macOS distribution alone does not prove current flat-only host XR support.
features.deliverable: native XR compatibility spec and evidence plan

features.description: Demonstrate optional XR inspection/control on one identified native game session.
acceptance_criteria: Connect the selected native host through the documented layer/proxy and verify identity, state read, frame capture and one bounded input/pose action.
Test disconnect/reconnect and prevent targeting another live app; unsupported tools remain explicit and input/session state is restored.
Keep the live viewport functional through its own surface provider and keep flat-mode orchestrator use independent of Operator; preserve native manual/device gates.
features.deliverable: XR adapter and real native runtime evidence

features.description: Complete the first desktop workflow with a terminal, editor, session browser and flat game tab.
acceptance_criteria: On macOS and Windows execute the empty-to-split workflow with multiple roots, ordinary and optional Vim editing, local draft recovery with explicit saves, real terminals and flat NOLF in a new tab.

Move and detach views, find retained sessions in the browser, reattach after GUI restart, and explicitly stop the intended game/process; identical filenames and similarly named sessions across roots never redirect a file write or session operation.
Record real rendered/input evidence and agreed performance measurements; a layout mock, terminal-only shell or external game window cannot close this milestone.
features.deliverable: docs/evidence/desktop-v0.md and packaged desktop builds

features.description: Specify the shared 2D Quest client delivery and desktop-link proof.
acceptance_criteria: Use official Android-panel/PWA paths and distinguish future Spatial SDK panes; select package/origin/sidecar constraints for the agreed 2D-first experience.
Specify desktop-owned files/builds/PTYs/agents and paired session/text/frame/input channels, including readable editor/terminal UI and keyboard/controller behavior.
Plan actual headset tests against Mac and Windows sidecars with latency/reconnect budgets; store distribution and native Quest-game coexistence remain separate claims.

features.description: Expose paired remote session access for the Quest client through the desktop sidecar.
acceptance_criteria: Pair a client with an explicit desktop and root scope and transport session lifecycle, terminal and file operations over an authenticated connection; resolve desktop root/session IDs without converting paths into Quest-local locations.
Test reconnect/duplicate requests, client revocation and wrong-session commands without duplicating processes or exposing unrelated project state.
Exercise the service on both Mac and Windows; credentials/configuration stay on the owning desktop and incompatible protocol versions fail explicitly.

features.description: Build the Quest 2D workspace client with real remote terminal and editor access.
acceptance_criteria: Build/install the selected client package and connect to both a Mac and a Windows sidecar on a real Quest.
Use the shared split/tab layout with tree/previews/basic editing and a real remote terminal; verify keyboard, pointer/controller, scrolling and text readability.
Verify connection loss/recovery and session browser behavior; layout persistence is independent of later spatial-panel support.

features.description: Display and interact with a desktop game in the Quest workspace pane.
acceptance_criteria: Render the selected actual desktop game stream into a Quest tab with correct session identity and input routing.
Move/resize/reconnect the view without relaunch; measure agreed latency, frame/decode cost and sustained interaction on both sidecar platforms.
Do not claim native Quest VR-game coexistence or headset parity from a desktop flat-game stream; record supported profiles and next limitations.

features.description: Qualify unmodified external-app presentation on a finite Mac/Windows app set.
acceptance_criteria: Separate cooperative adapters, captured/controlled windows and Windows reparenting; choose representative apps and approved platform APIs for the proof.
Test actual pixels plus input/focus, DPI/resize, dialogs, minimize/occlusion, app restart and permission denial; distinguish view-only from interactive support.
Publish a per-app/platform capability matrix and remote-client implications, not a universal embedding guarantee.

features.description: Provide the session browser for inspecting, reattaching and explicitly stopping sessions.
acceptance_criteria: List live/detached/exited sessions with explicit project/worktree root, type, target, state and attached-view information; distinguish similarly named sessions and retain root association even after its removal from the layout.
Attach or focus an existing session and explicitly stop one with accurate exit reporting; moving/closing the browser does not stop other sessions.

Exercise detached game and terminal sessions across GUI restart on macOS and Windows, including a stale/dead session and two similarly named worktrees; attach and Stop affect only the selected root/session.
